problems.title: Verify the two-square product identity
problems.question: Prove (a²+b²)(c²+d²)=(ac+bd)²+(ad-bc)².
problems.idea: Expand the right side and cancel its mixed terms.
steps: The mixed terms cancel. Group the remainder as a²(c²+d²)+b²(c²+d²).
problems.answer: The identity holds for all real a,b,c,d.

problems.title: Inverse-proportional addends
problems.question: Split 13 into addends inversely proportional to 2,3,4.
steps: Each unit is 1, so the addends are 6,4,3.

problems.title: Four factorization patterns
problems.question: Factor: (a)4x³y³-8x²y²; (b)30ax-34bx-15a+17b; (c)27a⁶-b³; (d)x²+4xy+4y²-4m²-12mn-9n².
problems.idea: Choose common factors, grouping, or standard identities.

problems.title: A sum of real squares must vanish termwise
problems.question: Solve (x+2y)²-6x-12y+9+(2x+y-3)²=0.
formulas: u²-6u+9=(u-3)²; two nonnegative squares sum to zero only if each is zero.

problems.title: Parallel line through a line intersection
problems.question: Find the line through the intersection of y=3x+4 and y=x+2, parallel to the line through (2,1),(1,-1).
problems.idea: Find the point and slope separately.

problems.title: Equal distances versus equal times
problems.question: Two cars cover 432 km. Car I drives half the distance at 108 km/h and half at 72. Car II drives half its time at each speed. Which arrives first, and by how long?
problems.idea: The two averaging methods give different total times.
formulas: For equal distances, T=D/(2v₁)+D/(2v₂); for equal times, average speed=(v₁+v₂)/2.
steps: Car II averages 90 km/h, taking 432/90=4.8 hours.

problems.title: A bisector in a 36–72–72 triangle
problems.question: Triangle angles have ratio 1:2:2. The least side is 3. Find the bisector from either largest-angle vertex.
problems.idea: Look at the subtriangle containing the short side.
formulas: Triangle angles sum to 180°; equal angles have equal opposite sides.
steps: The angles are 36°,72°,72°. Label A=36°,B=C=72°; then BC=3.
Bisect B by BD. In triangle BCD the angles are 36°,72°,72°.
Thus BD=BC=3, since both oppose 72° angles.

problems.title: An integer length bounded by triangle inequalities
problems.question: The perpendicular bisector of AB meets side AC at D. Triangle BCD has perimeter 2. AB is a positive integer. Find AB.
problems.idea: D is equally far from A and B.
steps: Hence 0<AB<2. The only positive integer is 1.

problems.title: Prove an exterior angle is bisected
problems.question: A,B,C,D lie on a circle in that order with CAD=CDA=70°. Prove BC bisects the angle adjacent to ABD.
problems.idea: Use the arcs opposite the given angles.
formulas: An inscribed angle equals half its intercepted arc; cyclic opposite angles are supplementary.
steps: In triangle ACD, ACD=40°. Thus ABD=40°, because both subtend arc AD.
ABC and ADC are opposite cyclic angles, so ABC=180°-70°=110°.
DBC=ABC-ABD=70°. The angle from BC to the ray opposite BA is 180°-ABC=70°.
These two equal angles divide the exterior angle adjacent to ABD.
problems.answer: BC bisects the exterior angle adjacent to ABD.

problems.title: Compare altitude, bisector and median feet
problems.question: In right ABC, A=15°,B=75°,C=90°. CH is the altitude, CL the bisector and CM the median to AB. Prove 2HL=LM.
problems.idea: Express all three feet as distances from A along the hypotenuse c.
formulas: AH=AC²/c; AL=c·AC/(AC+BC); AM=c/2; AC=c cos15°, BC=c sin15°.
steps: The bisector theorem gives AL=c cos15°/(cos15°+sin15°)=c(3+√3)/6.
